prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0072: DRAW’s dynamic weather avoidance function detects the weather conflict, which in turn triggers DRAW to calculate a route correction around the weather and post it on the DRAW Advisory List.
U0073: The proposed reroute around the weather and the corresponding STA and delay are shown in magenta in Figure 6.
U0074: DRAW calculates a reroute to avoid the conflict and return to the currently assigned STAR, if possible.
U0075: If returning to the current STAR is not possible, DRAW will attempt to reroute the flight to the most efficient weather-free alternate STAR.
U0076: The minimum user defined time-savings criteria described in 4.2.1 does not apply in this case because avoiding weather takes precedence over saving time.
U0077: Figure 6: DRAW Route Correction for Weather 4.3 DRAW PROCEDURES The DRAW system is a decision support tool for TMCs and does not change the current procedures by which reroutes are implemented in the NAS.
U0078: Figure 7 depicts a notional coordination procedure for implementing a DRAW route advisory.
U0079: Using the DRAW system, the TMC selects a DRAW route advisory from the DRAW Advisory List.
U0080: In doing so, the advised DRAW route(s) is loaded into the integrated route and schedule trial planner so that the TMC can evaluate before implementing.
U0081: The DRAW trial planner provides functionality for the user to modify and evaluate the route being trial planned as desired.
U0082: The TMC would then coordinate (via adjacent Center TMU, if necessary) with the Area Supervisor who would in turn coordinate with the appropriate sector controller to implement the reroute.
U0083: Figure 7 also shows alternate means of rerouting should Airborne Reroute (ABRR) and/or Data Comm become available: mechanisms that DRAW would employ to relay reroutes to the controller’s En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM) display and to digitally communicate reroutes to the flight crew, respectively.
U0084: Figure 7: Notional Reroute Procedure for DRAW Advisories 4.3.1 Reroute Coordination While DRAW does not introduce new procedures for implementing reroutes, the way in which current procedures are utilized to coordinate reroutes may impact the viability of the DRAW tool and/or the extent of its use.
U0085: The level and extent of required coordination is determined by the operational constraints on reroutes and the facilities involved in imposing those constraints.
U0086: Three levels of required coordination are considered here: Intra-Facility Coordination, Tier-One Facility Precoordination, and Multi-facility Coordination.
U0087: Intra-Facility Coordination: Some reroutes (e.g., those internal to the ‘home’ TBFM ARTCC) require no inter-facility coordination and can be coordinated with relative ease between the TMU, area supervisors and controllers within the same ARTCC (even for individual or small groups of flights).
U0088: Personnel within the same facility are likely to already be aware of key operational constraints on arrivals and be able to effectively assess/modify proposed weather avoidance reroutes.
U0089: Such coordination could be achieved via telephone between TMCs and Area Supervisors and verbally between Area Supervisors and Controllers.
U0090: Tier-One-Facility Precoordination: When flights are rerouted while located in an adjacent Center’s airspace, coordination with that facility is required since TMCs in the ‘home’ ARTCC may not be aware of operational constraints in the adjacent facility that would preclude a proposed reroute.
U0091: A number of methods have been proposed by TMC participants for precoordinated DRAW reroutes across facility boundaries.
U0092: For example, by precoordinating navaids/sectors and preferred arrival transition routing for flights arriving from a given flow (e.g., DFW arrivals from Chicago area), real-time inter-facility coordination for individual reroutes may be largely eliminated and replaced by perishable agreements that ‘grease the skids’ for near-term reroutes.
U0093: This method of precoordination would require input from sectors/areas to the TMCs coordinating the reroute plan.
U0094: This approach is analogous to a more tactical/dynamic playbook rerouting.
U0095: Alternatively, each facility would be responsible for rerouting as necessary to avoid weather and meet internal operational constraints while meeting agreed-upon inter-facility boundary conditions.
U0096: The extent to which boundary conditions can be precoordinated (e.g., telecon or Letter of Agreement) is a topic for further research.
U0097: Multi-Facility Coordination: Coordination of reroutes across multiple facilities could be managed in real time (without precoordination) either manually or supported by electronic requests/approval.
